claims.text: An MTP trained on TaVCrW DFT data can replace the EAM reference potential while FEP replaces thermodynamic integration.
The MTP+FEP approach will reduce computational cost by more than 80% relative to TOR-TILD.
The MTP+FEP approach will maintain a free-energy error below 0.5 meV/atom.
Solid-phase SRO stabilizes TaVCrW by approximately 2–3 meV/atom.
TaVCrW is a disordered BCC solid solution near its melting point.
Near-melting TaVCrW exhibits SRO stabilization over 2000–2400 K.
A supercell containing more than 1000 atoms is sufficient or necessary to resolve the SRO contribution without masking it through finite-size error.
The calculations will use GGA-PBE electronic structure data over 2000–2400 K.
Accurate reproduction of the ab initio phase-space distributions of both solid and liquid TaVCrW is the structural mediator enabling valid FEP sampling.
Capturing the local atomic environments responsible for SRO is necessary for the MTP to reproduce the claimed 2–3 meV/atom stabilization.
The MTP acts as a computationally efficient surrogate for the DFT energy landscape and permits more extensive sampling.
FEP can bypass the slow convergence of thermodynamic integration when calculating the solid–liquid free-energy difference.
Accurate results require the MTP to model electronic effects associated with DOS-gap shifts.
The predicted TaVCrW melting temperature will be within 10 K of the TOR-TILD result.
The TOR-TILD baseline uses an EAM reference potential and thermodynamic integration.
The method is valid only when supercell size resolves SRO and the 2000–2400 K range does not activate unrepresented magnetic or electronic effects.
Empirical GGA-PBE/LDA underbinding or overbinding rules fail for V and Cr at 0 K, and the resulting errors may propagate to the high-temperature liquid.
Neglected high-temperature magnetic fluctuations could shift the melting point by tens of kelvin.
The MTP's generalization to the complex TaVCrW liquid phase-space distribution has not been verified.
The hypothesis is falsified if MTP+FEP differs from TOR-TILD by more than 0.5 meV/atom or fails to reduce computational time by at least 80% at equal statistical convergence.

contradictions.description: TaVCrW contains four named elements and is consistently treated as that alloy elsewhere, but the uncertainty field calls it a 'quinary system.'
